policies.name: Digital Trade Strategy
policies.description: Australia's Digital Trade Strategy states that digital trade and digital technologies 'have the potential to level the playing field and promote inclusive growth by unlocking opportunities, new technologies and markets to MSMEs, women-run businesses and others...'. The Strategy also refers to Australia's aid for trade investment initiatives promoting the use of digital technologies to make trade more inclusive, supporting the uptake of e-commerce to make trade cheaper, more efficient and more accessible to disadvantaged groups, including women.

policies.name: Working for Women: A Strategy for Gender Equality
policies.description: Working for Women: A Strategy for Gender Equality provides a national framework for advancing gender equality across policy areas, including economic participation and workforce outcomes, while gender responsive budgeting supports the integration of gender considerations into policy development and decision-making across government.

policies.name: gender responsive budgeting (GRB)
policies.description: Since 2022, Australia has reintroduced gender responsive budgeting (GRB) as a tool to strengthen the integration of gender considerations into government decision-making. GRB aims to identify how policies, programs and expenditure decisions may affect women and men differently, helping to ensure policy outcomes are more equitable.

policies.name: 2023-2030 Australian Cyber Security Strategy
policies.description: These themes are reflected across Working for Women: A Strategy for Gender Equality and the 2023-2030 Australian Cyber Security Strategy, which note the importance of a more inclusive cyber workforce, especially for women.

policies.name: Statement on the Pathway to Diversity in STEM Review
policies.description: The Statement on the Pathway to Diversity in STEM Review highlights the importance of increasing participation of women and people from other underrepresented cohorts in STEM education and careers and outlines the government's broad actions to achieve this, while measures such as the Building Women's Careers Program are designed to improve women's access to training and work opportunities in sectors including digital and technology.

policies.name: Building Women's Careers Program
policies.description: For example, the Building Women's Careers program aims to drive structural and cultural change to improve women's access to flexible, safe and inclusive training and work opportunities in male-dominated industries, including digital and technology, thereby strengthening women's participation in digital trade. It creates partnerships between government, industry, employers, women's services and training providers to ensure women with access to work opportunities in target industries. Seven digital and technology-focused projects are being funded under the program.

policies.name: National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Plan
policies.description: Building digital and business capability is central, supported by the National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Plan and the National Skills Agreement, alongside actions under the Statement on the Pathway to Diversity in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) Review to strengthen women's participation in STEM and digital careers.

policies.name: National Skills Agreement
policies.description: Domestically, Australia delivers ongoing training and capability-building across digital and emerging technologies. This includes support for digital and AI skills, workforce transition and broader STEM participation. Relevant public initiatives include the National Skills Agreement, Fee-Free Technical and Further Education (TAFE), the Building Women's Careers Program, and the STEM Equity Monitor, which supports stronger evidence and accountability for diversity outcomes.

policies.name: Fee-Free Technical and Further Education (TAFE)
policies.description: Domestically, Australia delivers ongoing training and capability-building across digital and emerging technologies. This includes support for digital and AI skills, workforce transition and broader STEM participation. Relevant public initiatives include the National Skills Agreement, Fee-Free Technical and Further Education (TAFE), the Building Women's Careers Program, and the STEM Equity Monitor, which supports stronger evidence and accountability for diversity outcomes.

policies.name: Women in STEM and Entrepreneurship grants program
policies.description: Domestically, Australia's skills ecosystem increasingly covers both foundational and advanced digital capabilities. The National AI Plan emphasises support and training for Australians, while the Statement on the Pathway to Diversity in STEM Review highlights measures such as the Women in STEM and Entrepreneurship grants program, Science in Australia Gender Equity (SAGE), the National Skills Agreement and Building Women's Careers to strengthen women's participation in the pipeline for digital and technology roles.

policies.name: Science in Australia Gender Equity (SAGE)
policies.description: Domestically, Australia's skills ecosystem increasingly covers both foundational and advanced digital capabilities. The National AI Plan emphasises support and training for Australians, while the Statement on the Pathway to Diversity in STEM Review highlights measures such as the Women in STEM and Entrepreneurship grants program, Science in Australia Gender Equity (SAGE), the National Skills Agreement and Building Women's Careers to strengthen women's participation in the pipeline for digital and technology roles.

policies.name: Elevate: Boosting Diversity in STEM
policies.description: Women are included across innovation, STEM and entrepreneurship measures. These include Women in STEM and Entrepreneurship, SAGE, Elevate: Boosting Diversity in STEM, and broader digital and AI capability measures under the National AI Plan.

policies.name: STEM Equity Monitor
policies.description: Australia is strengthening data collection and monitoring relating to workforce participation and diversity, including through the STEM Equity Monitor. Targeted data and monitoring work is underway, although Australia does not maintain a single regular national collection covering all aspects of digital trade on a sex-disaggregated basis.

policies.name: 'Landing Pads' initiative
policies.description: Austrade's 'Landing Pads' initiative is designed to help tech scaleups:
items: make informed decisions about international expansion
develop and validate market-entry plans
connect with opportunities, customers, partners and funding to grow sales internationally
raise brand profile - including at iconic global trade shows.

policies.name: Go Global Toolkit
policies.description: The Australian government's Go Global Toolkit is a trade market intelligence, information and export capability platform that is available for Australian exporters, including women entrepreneurs, to access 24/7. The Toolkit contains information and insights on how to assess, find and prepare products or services for new markets.

policies.name: Free Trade Agreement (FTA) Portal
policies.description: Support is provided through practical measures that improve export capability and reduce friction at the border. This includes digital trade facilitation work through Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), including Australia's support for the Principles for the Interoperability of Electronic Invoicing Systems, as well as trade information services such as the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) Portal.

policies.name: Principles for the Interoperability of Electronic Invoicing Systems
policies.description: This includes digital trade facilitation work through Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), including Australia's support for the Principles for the Interoperability of Electronic Invoicing Systems, as well as trade information services such as the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) Portal.

policies.name: Simplified Trade System
policies.description: Australia is advancing paperless trade, digital verification and more streamlined trade processes, including through the Simplified Trade System and Digital Verification Platform. These reforms support cheaper, faster and simpler trade.

policies.name: Digital Verification Platform
policies.description: Australia is advancing paperless trade, digital verification and more streamlined trade processes, including through the Simplified Trade System and Digital Verification Platform. These reforms support cheaper, faster and simpler trade.

policies.name: Australia-United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement (A-UKFTA)
policies.description: The Australia-United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement (A-UKFTA) expressly links women and digital trade in Chapter 14 (Digital Trade). Article 14.21 - Cooperation, paragraph 1(h), states: 'Parties shall endeavour to facilitate participation by women in digital trade, acknowledging the objectives in Chapter 24 (Trade and Gender Equality).'

policies.name: Australia-United Arab Emirates Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)
policies.description: The Australia-United Arab Emirates Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) also expressly links women and digital trade in Chapter 12 (Digital Trade). Article 12.25 (Digital Inclusion) paragraph 2, states: 'Parties shall cooperate on matters relating to digital inclusion, including the participation of women, rural populations, ...'.

policies.name: AANZFTA Second Protocol
policies.description: The upgraded Agreement Establishing the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Area (AANZFTA Second Protocol) includes a standalone Article 19 (Digital Inclusion for Electronic Commerce), which supports digital inclusion by recognising that all people and businesses should be able to participate in, contribute to, and benefit from electronic commerce and digital trade.

policies.name: Australia's International Gender Equality Strategy
policies.description: Australia's International Gender Equality Strategy states that Australia works with global partners to promote and mainstream gender and economic equality in trade agreements and policies, supporting women-led businesses, and driving reforms for workplace equality and financial inclusion.

policies.name: Australia's International Development Policy
policies.description: Australia's International Development Policy, launched in 2023, has a target of 80 per cent of all development investments to address gender equality effectively, and requires investments of 3 million Australian dollars (AUD) and above to include gender equality objectives.

policies.name: Invested: Australia's Southeast Asia Economic Strategy to 2040
policies.description: Chapter 10 of Invested: Australia's Southeast Asia Economic Strategy to 2040 acknowledges the critical role of digital trade in supporting MSMEs and women-led businesses, particularly in banking and e-commerce/retail sectors through the 'Digital Economy' chapter.

policies.name: Regional Trade for Development (RT4D)
policies.description: The Australia-New Zealand supported Regional Trade for Development (RT4D) initiative assists Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Member States to meet their commitments and realise the advantages offered by the Agreement Establishing the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Area (AANZFTA) and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP). It supports women in digital trade through the Trade and Gender Equality Incubator.

policies.name: eTrade for Women Initiative
policies.description: UNCTAD's eTrade for Women Initiative offers training to empower women digital entrepreneurs in developing and least developed countries to become more visible as role models and better heard by policymakers to foster change in the business enabling environment. Training is offered through eTrade for Women Masterclasses. Two Masterclasses have been held since 2024, one for South Asia participants (2024) and one for Southeast Asia and Pacific participants (2025).

policies.name: Trade Facilitation Support Program (TFSP)
policies.description: The World Bank's Trade Facilitation Support Program (TFSP) reduces the time, cost, and complexity of moving products across borders by streamlining processes through digitisation and automation. It supports women traders by addressing data gaps, modernising border infrastructure, and standardising cross-border logistics to reduce the unique regulatory and logistical obstacles women-led businesses face.

policies.name: Trade and Supply Chain Finance Program (TSCFP)
policies.description: The Asian Development Bank's (ADB) Trade and Supply Chain Finance Program (TSCFP) mobilises private capital and knowledge solutions to close market gaps, promote digitalisation, and support the reconfiguration of supply chains. Its Gender Initiative aims to close the persistent gender gap in international trade and finance by supporting women-led small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through targeted financing, networking platforms, and mentorship programs.

policies.name: Pacific E-commerce Initiative
policies.description: DFAT also supports the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat's (PIFS) Pacific E-commerce Initiative, which does not have activities that specifically target female digital traders, but rather integrates gender equality as a core, cross-cutting dimension into its Pacific Regional E-commerce Strategy and Roadmap.

policies.name: E-commerce Rules Course for Pacific Policymakers
policies.description: The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat's (PIFS) E-commerce Rules Course for Pacific Policymakers builds knowledge and capacity among Pacific policymakers on the structure, content, and strategic implications of e-commerce rules, equipping participants with a practical understanding of global and regional digital trade rulemaking and helping ensure that Pacific interests are effectively represented in current and future digital trade arrangements.

policies.name: TechCoop investment
policies.description: For example, the TechCoop investment arose from independent investment committee decisions to invest in a portfolio company that leverages digital infrastructure to facilitate trade, rather than from a direct policy link between support for women entrepreneurs and digital infrastructure for trade facilitation.

policies.name: Ministerial Council on Trade and Investment
policies.description: Australia also works with state and territory governments, where relevant, on the design and delivery of policies and programs that support women's economic participation, such as through the Ministerial Council on Trade and Investment.

policies.name: Programa Elas Exportam
policies.description: Um exemplo é o Programa Elas Exportam, iniciativa conjunta do Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC) e da Agência Brasileira de Promoção de Exportações e Investimentos (ApexBrasil), voltada ao fortalecimento das capacidades de mulheres empreendedoras para a internacionalização de seus negócios. O programa combina mentorias individuais, capacitações técnicas e desenvolvimento de competências socioemocionais, contemplando temas diretamente relacionados ao comércio digital e à economia digital. Entre as atividades oferecidas estão sessões coletivas sobre comércio eletrônico internacional e internacionalização de empresas por meio de plataformas digitais.

policies.name: Digital Transformation Strategy of the Republic of Bulgaria 2024-2030
policies.description: The Digital Transformation Strategy of the Republic of Bulgaria 2024-2030 (https://www.strategy.bg/bg/strategy-documents/1687 ) is a key strategic document developed by the former Ministry of e-Government, currently the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation, which includes a specific focus on women, indicating them as a key target group in several areas.

policies.name: National Program "Digital Bulgaria 2025"

policies.name: National Strategy for SMEs 2021-2027
policies.description: The National Strategy for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises contains measures aimed at supporting women in business. In the updated document, whose validity has been extended until 2030, women's entrepreneurship is identified as a specific priority for economic growth. The measures and support mechanisms set out in the strategy and the related programmes are focused on the following areas:
items: Specialised credit lines: Preferential financial products are offered through state institutions such as the Bulgarian Development Bank. One example is the programme "For Women Entrepreneurs", which supports women's entrepreneurship by providing long-term financial resources on favourable terms. The programme aims to promote women's economic activity, develop business potential and create employment.

Promotion of key types of entrepreneurship: Women's entrepreneurship is addressed alongside youth and family businesses under the priority "Promoting key types of entrepreneurship". The measures include financing, training and mentoring programmes for women who are starting or developing a business.

Support for digitalisation and e-commerce solutions: A priority measure in the National Strategy for SMEs is "Support for SMEs to implement and use e-commerce solutions - websites, electronic payments, mobile applications, internet security solutions, data storage, etc." The measure is aimed at promoting the digitalisation of business activities while also strengthening the digital skills of entrepreneurs.

policies.name: For Women Entrepreneurs
policies.description: One example is the programme "For Women Entrepreneurs", which supports women's entrepreneurship by providing long-term financial resources on favourable terms. The programme aims to promote women's economic activity, develop business potential and create employment.

policies.name: She's Next
policies.description: Visa's "She's Next" Programme in Bulgaria, Season 2025/2026: This initiative supports women-owned small businesses through financing, training and mentoring. In its second season, 15 finalists will receive mentoring on business strategy, finance, marketing and digitalisation, while three selected participants will be awarded financial grants of EUR 10,000, EUR 7,500 and EUR 5,000.

policies.name: Digital Clubs Project and Digital Awakener Campaign
policies.description: Digital Clubs Project and Digital Awakener Campaign, May-July 2026: The Ministry of Labour and Social Policy and the Employment Agency are developing a network of digital clubs across the country. The initiative gives priority to women, mothers on maternity leave and people in disadvantaged situations, providing free access to computers, the internet and mentors for acquiring basic and intermediate digital skills.

policies.name: Association of Women Entrepreneurs "Selena"
policies.description: Specialised e-commerce academies: Organisations such as the Association of Women Entrepreneurs "Selena" organise masterclasses on digital marketing, search engine optimisation and the use of payment tools, supporting women entrepreneurs in adapting to current requirements for online sales.

policies.name: National Mentoring Programme for Women Entrepreneurs
policies.description: Examples of such programmes include the National Mentoring Programme for Women Entrepreneurs and the F.A.M.E. (Female Founders, Angel Investors, Mentors and Explorers) Growth Programme.

policies.name: F.A.M.E. (Female Founders, Angel Investors, Mentors and Explorers) Growth Programme
policies.description: The F.A.M.E. Growth Programme is a three-month initiative designed for women entrepreneurs with an established business, as well as next-generation leaders in family-owned companies. It offers practical training, individual mentoring, access to experts and opportunities to build strategic partnerships.

policies.name: EXPORT BUILDERS
policies.description: The Bulgarian Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Agency provides significant support for women entrepreneurs to access international digital markets through its EXPORT BUILDERS training programme, which offers 20 online training sessions divided into 7 modules. The agency also organises participation in virtual trade fairs and provides direct expert support through mobile teams across the country.

policies.name: N-Spark
policies.description: The N-Spark initiative, in partnership with the World Bank, focuses on innovation management, AI, and automation.

policies.name: Bulgarian Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Agency
policies.description: The Bulgarian Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Agency provides various forms of market access support, including onboarding to e-commerce platforms (support for moving business online), export readiness training (EXPORT BUILDERS), digital marketing support (through various training programmes), product standards guidance, logistics support, market intelligence, and participation in virtual trade fairs. The agency also organises international exhibitions and B2B meetings.

policies.name: National Council for Equality between Women and Men
policies.description: The National Council for Equality between Women and Men and the National Action Plan for Promoting Equality between Women and Men provide a general coordination framework, although they are not specifically focused on digital trade.

policies.name: National Action Plan for Promoting Equality between Women and Men
policies.description: The National Council for Equality between Women and Men under the Council of Ministers coordinates monitoring in the field of gender equality through the annual National Action Plan and its implementation reports.

policies.name: EU Funds Monitoring System
policies.description: The EU Funds Monitoring System tracks beneficiary profiles and assesses whether investments support business sustainability and comply with EU horizontal principles, including gender equality.

policies.name: "Digitaliza tu Pyme"
policies.description: Women are indirectly involved in the digital transformation policy for Chilean SMEs through the "Digitaliza tu Pyme" (Digitalize Your SME) program, led by the Ministry of Economy, Development, and Tourism. While the program is not designed as a strategy exclusively for women, its current design incorporates gender as a cross-cutting inclusion criterion within a broader approach to reducing the digital divide in micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). "Digitaliza tu Pyme" supports MSMEs through the "Chequeo Digital" (Digital Maturity Self-Assessment) tool and connects them with training, technical assistance, and pathways for digital adoption. The updated 2025 strategy explicitly incorporated equity and inclusive access as guiding principles, aiming to ensure that the benefits of digitalization reach traditionally underserved groups, including women entrepreneurs, rural businesses, and other underserved segments.

policies.name: "Chequeo Digital"
policies.description: The programme uses "Chequeo Digital", an online self-assessment tool, to measure firms' digital maturity and guide them toward relevant support. This helps identify differences by sex, sector, territory and firm characteristics, and supports better targeting of training and assistance related to e-commerce, digital payments, digital marketing, cybersecurity, business management tools and technology adoption.

policies.name: "Pymes en Línea"
policies.description: For example, "Pymes en Línea" (SMEs Online), a public digital training initiative linked to the program, included training activities in 2022 and 2023 with a focus on women-led businesses.

policies.name: "Ruta Digital"
policies.description: A second priority is building digital and business skills. The programme connects firms to training platforms such as "Pymes en Línea" and "Ruta Digital", and uses the "Chequeo Digital" self-assessment tool to guide firms toward training pathways according to their level of digital maturity. This helps women entrepreneurs acquire practical capabilities in digital tools, business management, data use, cybersecurity, online sales and customer engagement.

policies.name: "Digitaliza tu Almacén"
policies.description: For example, "Digitaliza tu Almacén" supports neighbourhood stores and small retailers through grants, technical assistance and training for the adoption of point-of-sale systems, electronic invoicing, inventory management software, financial control tools and digital payment solutions.

policies.name: "Fortalecimiento de Capacidades Exportadoras para MiPymes de la Alianza del Pacífico mediante comercio electrónico transfronterizo"
policies.description: A concrete example is the project "Fortalecimiento de Capacidades Exportadoras para MiPymes de la Alianza del Pacífico mediante comercio electrónico transfronterizo", implemented within the Pacific Alliance framework with support from SUBREI, ProChile and ECLAC. The initiative seeks to strengthen MSMEs' export capacities through cross-border e-commerce and includes firms led by both women and men. The "Digitaliza tu Pyme" team supports this initiative from the MSME digitalisation perspective.

policies.name: "Mujer Exporta"
policies.description: Export promotion services are provided through ProChile, including "Mujer Exporta", which supports women-led companies that are exporters or mature enough to export through training, networks, empowerment activities and commercial promotion.

policies.name: "Inicia" and "Expande" calls
policies.description: Corfo has opened "Inicia" and "Expande" calls for innovative ventures led by women, supporting projects from early validation stages to expansion into new markets.

policies.name: "Semilla Inicia para Empresas Lideradas por Mujeres"
policies.description: For example, "Semilla Inicia" para Empresas Lideradas por Mujeres supports innovative ventures led by women through co-financing, technical and commercial validation, mentoring and entrepreneurial skills development.

policies.name: "Female Founder Factor"
policies.description: Start-Up Chile, Corfo's public startup accelerator, also includes gender-focused measures through "Female Founder Factor". This initiative seeks to empower women in the entrepreneurial ecosystem and is connected to programmes such as "Build", "Ignite" and "Growth", which include gender parity objectives or preferential funding conditions for startups with women leaders.

policies.name: Global Trade and Gender Arrangement
policies.description: Chile has promoted gender equality in trade through gender and trade chapters in trade agreements, participation in international initiatives such as the Global Trade and Gender Arrangement and the Inclusive Trade Action Group, and public-private coordination on inclusive trade. These instruments aim to reduce barriers faced by women, MSMEs and other underrepresented groups in international trade.

policies.name: Inclusive Trade Action Group
policies.description: Chile has promoted gender equality in trade through gender and trade chapters in trade agreements, participation in international initiatives such as the Global Trade and Gender Arrangement and the Inclusive Trade Action Group, and public-private coordination on inclusive trade. These instruments aim to reduce barriers faced by women, MSMEs and other underrepresented groups in international trade.

policies.name: digital platform to connect supply and demand from women-led companies
policies.description: More recently, UN Women, ProChile and Corfo announced the development of a digital platform to connect supply and demand from women-led companies, aiming to improve their participation in national and international value chains.

policies.name: "ChileB2B"
policies.description: In addition, Chile has public platform-based initiatives such as "ChileB2B" and new efforts led by UN Women, ProChile and Corfo to connect supply and demand from women-led companies.

policies.name: Law 1341 of 2009
policies.description: Law 1341 of 2009 establishes that the State will intervene in the information and communications technology sector to achieve goals such as promoting access to ICTs, with the ultimate goal of universal service, the development of content and applications, the provision of services that use these technological tools and the massification of e-Government, and to encourage and promote the development of the information and communications technology industry to contribute to economic growth, competitiveness, job creation and exports.

policies.name: National Development Plan 2022-2026 (Law 2294 of 2023)
policies.description: The project aligns with the guidelines of the National Development Plan 2022-2026 (Law 2294 of 2023), which defines digital transformation as a cross-cutting axis of productive development and proposes the digitization of business processes as a mechanism to overcome structural barriers to market access.

policies.name: "Technology for Life" initiative
policies.description: The "Technology for Life" initiative emphasizes that promoting e-commerce is fundamental for the democratization of ICTs and the reduction of inequalities.

policies.name: National Reindustrialization Policy (CONPES 4129 of 2023)
policies.description: Likewise, the project is aligned with the National Reindustrialization Policy (CONPES 4129 of 2023), which highlights the need to connect small producers with new markets through digital platforms, emphasizing the role of agribusiness as one of the country's priority productive sectors.

policies.name: National Digital Strategy (END) 2023-2026
policies.description: Additionally, the project is aligned with the National Digital Strategy (END) 2023-2026, launched in February 2024, which aims to expand the use of ICTs, close the urban-rural divide, and strengthen digital skills.

policies.name: National Artificial Intelligence Policy (CONPES 4144 of 2025)
policies.description: It also addresses the guidelines of the National Artificial Intelligence Policy (CONPES 4144 of 2025), which recognizes that the use of emerging technologies such as AI in SMEs remains limited and must be actively promoted, especially in strategic sectors such as agriculture.

policies.name: Tu Negocio en Línea - TNL
policies.description: Your Online Business - TNL prepared people to learn how to use AI to create their page where beneficiaries offered their products or services online, as well as other sessions taught them to acquire skills in digital marketing, online payments, business management, among others.

policies.name: Fondo Mujer Libre y Productiva
policies.description: In Colombia, the main actors supporting women's participation in digital trade include the Ministry of Information and Communications Technologies (MinTIC), the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Tourism (MinCIT), Fondo Mujer Libre y Productiva, iNNpulsa Colombia, APPS.CO, ProColombia, Bancóldex, SENA-Fondo Emprender, the Colombian Chamber of Electronic Commerce, regional chambers of commerce and local economic development agencies. International and private-sector partners include the Inter-American Development Bank and Mujeres ConnectAmericas, the International Trade Centre's SheTrades initiative, Google, IBM, Visa and Mastercard. Their support includes digital-skills training, e-commerce adoption, access to finance, business mentoring, digital payments, participation in online marketplaces and connection with international buyers.

policies.name: National Plan for the Promotion of Exports of the Dominican Republic 2020-2030
policies.description: National Plan for the Promotion of Exports of the Dominican Republic 2020-2030 Pillar 1/ Measures 1.1.1.3. Develop a strategy to increase women's participation in the chain of prioritized export goods and services, favoring equity and women's empowerment. 1.1.1.4. Support for entrepreneurial initiatives for the export of goods and services, supported by training, mentoring, technical assistance, linkage and financing programs through the planning of the resources available for the promotion of exports, such as e-commerce, digital marketing and appropriate delivery logistics.

policies.name: National Development Strategy of the Dominican Republic 2030 (Law 1-12)
policies.description: National Development Strategy of the Dominican Republic 2030 (Law 1-12) Article 12. Gender Approach. In accordance with this law, all plans, programs, projects and public policies must incorporate the gender approach in their respective areas of action. Lines of action: 3.4.2.5 Develop training programs that encourage the insertion of women in non-traditional sectors, and take into account the balance of productive and reproductive work. 3.4.2.7 Promote the use of information and communication technologies as a tool to expand the scope of vocational and technical training.

policies.name: National Strategy for the Export of Modern Services (ENESM)
policies.description: Through initiatives such as the National Strategy for the Export of Modern Services (ENESM), MICM promotes the internationalization of knowledge-intensive and creative sectors, including digital content, audiovisual production, animation, videogames, design and consulting services.

policies.name: National Strategy for Women Exporters
policies.description: This coordinated approach is reflected in initiatives such as the Women in Exports studies, the National Strategy for Women Exporters, the SheTrades Hub Dominican Republic, and capacity-building programmes that strengthen women's digital and export capabilities.

policies.name: Women Exporters in the Digital Economy (WEIDE) Fund
policies.description: A key example is the Women Exporters in the Digital Economy (WEIDE) Fund, implemented by the International Trade Centre (ITC) and the World Trade Organization (WTO), which supports women-led businesses in adopting digital technologies, strengthening digital and entrepreneurial skills, expanding access to e-commerce and digital platforms, and increasing their participation in global value chains.

policies.name: MIPYMES Mujer Certification
policies.description: Through programmes such as the MIPYMES Mujer Certification and projects supporting creative industries and startups, the Ministry promotes greater visibility, formalization and scalability of women-owned businesses.

policies.name: Women in Exports study
policies.description: ProDominicana has published six editions of its Women in Exports study (2021-2025), which analyze the performance, challenges and opportunities of women-led exporting firms in the Dominican Republic. The studies consistently identify the productive use of digital technologies, including digital marketing, e-commerce, digital business management tools and access to digital trade information, as key enablers of internationalization, particularly for women-led SMEs. They also highlight the need to strengthen digital skills and technology adoption to improve competitiveness, market access and participation in the digital economy.

policies.name: "Women in Exports" dashboard

policies.name: National Strategy for Women Entrepreneurs (ENME)
policies.description: In particular, the National Strategy for Women Entrepreneurs (ENME) stablished by the Supreme Decree No. 012-2022-MIMP, provides a multisectoral framework to strengthen the economic opportunities and capacities of women entrepreneurs and business owners. Following its amendment by Supreme Decree No. 007-2025-MIMP, the strategy incorporates several elements related to digitalization. For example, the amendment aims to facilitate women leaders of micro, small and medium enterprises to access technological tools applicable to their businesses and encourages the use of e-commerce and virtual channels that allow women-led businesses can become more competitive.
items: In particular, Component 2, "Market Access," includes the development of commercial and logistics capabilities in both physical and digital environments, as well as the diversification of sales channels and efforts to strengthen the competitiveness of products and services offered by women entrepreneurs. Component 4, "Capacity-Building," also includes actions aimed at developing digital skills.

In addition, Component 5, "Access to Finance," promotes the use of digital channels to help reduce transaction costs and improve women's access to financial products and services. policies.name: National Gender Equality Policy (PNIG)
policies.description: From the perspective of Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations (MIMP), these objectives are framed by the National Gender Equality Policy (PNIG), particularly Priority Objective 4, which focuses on guaranteeing women's economic and social rights, and are linked to the National Strategy for Women Entrepreneurs (ENME), which promotes the participation of women who lead businesses and entrepreneurial ventures.

policies.name: National Digital Transformation Policy
policies.description: The National Digital Transformation Policy, led by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, also contributes to strengthening the economic empowerment of women business owners by promoting access to and effective use of digital technologies. These tools facilitate access to markets, financial services, information, training, and sales channels, helping improve women's productivity, competitiveness, and participation in the digital economy. Strengthening digital skills is also key to reducing gaps in the business sector.

policies.name: National Multisectoral Foreign Trade Policy to 2040 (PNMCE)
policies.description: In respect of Priority Objective 5: "Strengthen collaborative environments for the development of foreign trade companies' activities" of the National Multisectoral Foreign Trade Policy to 2040, this includes guidelines for the digital transformation of companies and the use of e-commerce. Likewise, Priority Objective 2: "Optimize foreign trade operations through trade facilitation measures for foreign trade users in the country" and "Improve foreign trade facilitation" includes guidelines on the simplification, harmonization, and modernization of customs and logistics procedures, the digitization of processes, the application of risk management criteria and greater regulatory transparency. These guidelines translate into services that include interventions through technical assistance and training programmes.

policies.name: "Ella Exporta" Programme for Leading Women Entrepreneurs
policies.description: First, the "Ella Exporta" Programme for Leading Women Entrepreneurs, implemented since 2017, is a women-only capacity-building programme aimed at narrowing the gender gap in Peru's export sector. Its curriculum includes an E-Commerce module at Basic Level, which covers basic concepts of digital commerce, and a social media and Digital Platforms module at Advanced Level. Within these modules, participants are also informed about PROMPERÚ's institutional e-commerce programme, so that women entrepreneurs who wish to move beyond introductory content have a clear pathway into specialized assistance.

policies.name: "E-Commerce Programme"
policies.description: Second, PROMPERÚ implements an "E-Commerce Programme", a general instrument - not gender-specific - designed to increase and diversify exports through digital channels. It is aimed at SMEs in the food, apparel, jewelry, gift items and home decoration sectors. Its objective is to train and assist companies throughout the process of entering, positioning and consolidating their value-added products on global e-commerce platforms, taking advantage of the commercial opportunities offered by international markets. According to historical participation records, women entrepreneurs represent 57% of total participants in this programme.

policies.name: "Cross-Border E-Commerce for MSMEs Among Pacific Alliance Countries"
policies.description: In addition, as part of the Pacific Alliance's Technical Group on SMEs and Entrepreneurship, Peru have been implementing the project "Cross-Border E-Commerce for MSMEs Among Pacific Alliance Countries" to strengthen the capacities of micro, small, and medium-sized exporting enterprises in Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru, in order to facilitate their entry into cross-border e-commerce within the Pacific Alliance. The project aims for 50% of participating companies to be led by women.

policies.name: "Acceleration of Innovative and Sustainable Businesses in the Pacific Alliance - BioEmprende"
policies.description: Likewise, within the framework of the Pacific Alliance's Technical Group n Science, Technology, and Innovation, the project "Acceleration of Innovative and Sustainable Businesses in the Pacific Alliance - BioEmprende" is being implemented, which seeks to strengthen capacities and foster connections to enhance the competitiveness of bioeconomy businesses, thereby contributing to the consolidation of this sector as a driver of sustainable economic development within the Pacific Alliance. The project does not have a gender quota for business participation; however, there are companies led by women participating in the project.

policies.name: Women Entrepreneur Platform
policies.description: Through the Women Entrepreneur Platform, the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations (MIMP) provides a digital space to share information on services and opportunities aimed at supporting the development of women entrepreneurs. One of its features is the Women Entrepreneur Catalogue, which currently showcases and promotes 266 products offered by women entrepreneurs. However, the catalogue currently serves mainly an informational and promotional purpose, as it does not allow users to complete transactions or make online payments directly through the platform.

policies.name: ConnectAmericas platform
policies.description: There are also examples of the MIMP working with digital tools aimed at international trade. In 2020, for instance, MIMP promoted the ConnectAmericas platform among women business owners. The platform enables users to strengthen their business and digital skills, participate in virtual business matchmaking events, and establish international business connections.

policies.name: Peru Marketplace
policies.description: In respect of Ministry of Foreign Trade and Tourism (MINCETUR) has made the Peru Marketplace, platform available to companies-a virtual B2B marketplace that connects international buyers with exporters who list their exportable products in their online stores. Peru Marketplace is a strategic tool for the international positioning of Peruvian export products.

policies.name: CyberWow
policies.description: The Ministry of Production (PRODUCE) reported that more than 1,500 MSEs from across the country participated in the 2025 editions of CyberWow, generating over PEN 1.4 million in sales across sectors such as textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, food and beverages, handicrafts, fashion, beauty, and tourism.

policies.name: "Thursdays for Women Entrepreneurs"
policies.description: Under the ENME, MIMP implements the "Thursdays for Women Entrepreneurs" initiative, which aims to strengthen the capacities of women entrepreneurs and business owners through in-person and virtual training sessions, in coordination with public and private institutions and regional governments. The initiative includes content related to digital entrepreneurship, business digitalization, e-commerce, and digital marketing.

policies.name: Foreign Trade Capacity-Building Program
policies.description: To that end, the Foreign Trade Capacity-Building Program is being promoted and aims to strengthen participants' capabilities in areas related to foreign trade, as well as to provide practical tools that enable them to improve their competitiveness and enter international markets more effectively. Similarly, it seeks to promote and consolidate a culture of exporting nationwide, creating greater opportunities for more Peruvian companies to participate in international trade. This programme is not exclusively for women, but it does welcome their participation. Among the topics covered, it includes e-commerce and cross-border trade.

policies.name: "MYPE Digital"
policies.description: As an additional reference, PRODUCE also runs the "MYPE Digital" initiative, which offers online courses, workshops, and in-person or virtual advisory services on e-commerce, digital payments, digital marketing, data analysis, and process automation.

policies.name: E-PYMEX
policies.description: In respect of MINCETUR, it offers training in the form of webinars or workshops. In particular, it has developed training programs focused on the digital management of foreign trade documents, such as E-PYMEX; traceability and security in the export supply chain; artificial intelligence in export logistics; the digital transformation of export logistics; and logistics for e-commerce, among others.

policies.name: Multisectoral Executive Working Group for Strengthening the Economic Empowerment of Women Entrepreneurs and Microbusiness Owners
policies.description: One of the main coordination mechanisms is the Multisectoral Executive Working Group for Strengthening the Economic Empowerment of Women Entrepreneurs and Microbusiness Owners, which brings together the MIMP and sectors such as Ministry of Production (PRODUCE), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), Ministry of Agrarian Development and Irrigation (MIDAGRI), Ministry of Development and Social Inclusion (MIDIS), Ministry of Foreign Trade and Tourism (MINCETUR), Ministry of Labor and Employment Promotion (MTPE), Ministry of Environment (MINAM), Presidency of the Council of Ministers (PCM), among others. The Working Group helps identify opportunities for joint action, coordinate activities, and promote the adaptation of public services to the needs of women entrepreneurs.

policies.name: Nominal Registry of Women Entrepreneurs and Business Owners (Padrón Nominal de Mujeres Emprendedoras y Empresarias)
policies.description: In addition, MIMP, through the National Strategy for Women Entrepreneurs (ENME), maintains the Nominal Registry of Women Entrepreneurs and Business Owners (Padrón Nominal de Mujeres Emprendedoras y Empresarias), which identifies and characterizes women who own or operate businesses. It collects information on personal and business profiles, including type of business, income, training needs, household responsibilities and other socioeconomic characteristics, and is used to connect registered women with training, market access initiatives and public and private business support services.

policies.name: Women's Economic Empowerment Support Centre (CAAEM)
policies.description: One example is the Women's Economic Empowerment Support Centre (CAAEM), where women entrepreneurs receive personalized support to strengthen their business management skills and improve their readiness to access financing opportunities. As part of this pathway, in 2026 the MIMP has been facilitating access to seed capital for CAAEM graduates to support the strengthening and growth of their businesses.

policies.name: "Women in Cross-Border Trade: A Case Study of Huaquillas-Aguas Verdes and Desaguadero"
policies.description: The project, entitled "Women in Cross-Border Trade: A Case Study of Huaquillas-Aguas Verdes and Desaguadero", was developed by Peru with the support of UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) to identify the main barriers and challenges faced by women engaged in cross-border trade. The project focused on the Peru-Ecuador border, particularly the Huaquillas-Aguas Verdes area, and the Peru-Bolivia border, particularly Desaguadero, gathering information directly from women traders and other stakeholders involved in border operations. The findings highlighted challenges related to access to information on foreign trade regulations and procedures, border infrastructure and conditions, and other factors affecting women's participation in cross-border trade.

As part of the strategy, measures are being implemented to foster interest in IT and engineering professions among girls and women, as well as to develop flexible forms of employment and digital entrepreneurship.
