More than 100 Russian companies participated in the Beauty Box "Made in Russia" project, with promotional efforts covering markets in the UAE, China, Uzbekistan, and CIS countries.

policies.name: Export School of JSC "Russian Export Center" (REC)
policies.description: REC hosts webinars on export e-commerce for both men and women. In 2026, the REC Export School, in collaboration with the REC Analytics Center, launched a series of four seminars on using AI tools for exporters. The REC Export School also includes modules on using AI tools for exporters in its acceleration programs, such as: market analysis using AI; competitive intelligence; and developing market entry strategies with digital tools.

policies.name: Digital Slovenia 2030
policies.description: Slovenia's national digital transformation framework, Digital Slovenia 2030, includes gender-related objectives in the area of digital skills and ICT professionals. Slovenia has set a national target of increasing the share of women among ICT specialists to 25% by 2030. Specific measures include reskilling programmes for women in ICT occupations and activities promoting the participation of girls and women in STEM and ICT.

policies.name: SPIRIT Slovenia (Slovenia Business Development Agency)
policies.description: In 2025, through SPIRIT Slovenia (Slovenia Business Development Agency), we started implementing 2 complementary measures, namely: 1. training and mentoring for the acquisition of entrepreneurial skills; and 2. providing financial resources to facilitate the start-up and initial operation of a company. The activities will run until 2029. Through various training and mentoring we contribute to raising entrepreneurship competences and encourage entrepreneurial activity with a view to harnessing the potential of young people up to 29 years of age and women. By providing financial incentives, we give businesses founded by young people up to 29 years of age and women access to a source of funding that helps them to overcome barriers in the start-up phase and thus increase their survival rate.

policies.name: reskilling programmes for women in ICT occupations
policies.description: Slovenia has implemented dedicated ICT reskilling programmes for women. Training areas have included artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data analysis, IT support. These programmes primarily address ICT and digital skills rather than e-commerce or cross-border digital trade specifically.

policies.name: Resolution on the National Programme for Equal Opportunities for Women and Men 2023-2030 (ReNPEMŽM23-30)
policies.description: Resolution on the National Programme for Equal Opportunities for Women and Men 2023-2030 (ReNPEMŽM23-30) = https://www.gov.si/assets/ministrstva/MDDSZ/Enake-moznosti/ReNPEMZM2030/ReNPEMZM23-30_EN.pdf

policies.name: 'Desafía San Francisco' programme
policies.description: One example is the 'Desafía San Francisco' programme, designed by ICEX, Red.es and the Spanish Economic and Commercial Office in Los Angeles, which has launched a new edition aimed exclusively at Spanish start-ups led by women, with the aim of helping them enter the US technology market.

policies.name: 'Internationalise in Feminine' program
policies.description: The 'Internationalise in Feminine' program by ICEX aims to provide market intelligence for international expansion by leveraging the expertise and local market knowledge of Spain's Network of Economic and Commercial Offices abroad.

policies.name: España-Latam Scale-UP
policies.description: Our programme España-Latam Scale-UP, an initiative of ICEX, BID LAB and Endeavor to attract Latin American scale-ups that aim to expand and establish themselves in Spain, as a gateway to the European market. A selected group of Latin American startups will participate in a week-long immersion programme in the Spanish entrepreneurial ecosystem. During the immersion they will be able to meet first-hand the main players: institutions, venture capital funds, corporations, accelerators and the experience of other startups operating global technology businesses from Spain. It pays special attention to startups led by women, among other areas.

policies.name: ICEX
policies.description: ICEX's main areas of action in support of women in 2025 were:
items: Promoting the visibility of female leadership.
Creating and strengthening women's business networks.
Supporting women-led technology entrepreneurship.
Producing market intelligence with a gender perspective.
Promoting women's participation in international events.
Developing gender-related indicators in internationalisation.
Implementing internal policies on equality and work-life balance.

policies.name: State Strategy for Ensuring Equal Rights and Opportunities for Women and Men until 2030
policies.description: Ukraine implements the State Strategy for Ensuring Equal Rights and Opportunities for Women and Men until 2030, as well as the National Action Plan for the implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1325 "Women, Peace and Security", both of which contribute to women's economic empowerment, including through entrepreneurship and digital inclusion.

policies.name: National Action Plan for the implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1325 "Women, Peace and Security"
policies.description: Ukraine implements the State Strategy for Ensuring Equal Rights and Opportunities for Women and Men until 2030, as well as the National Action Plan for the implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1325 "Women, Peace and Security", both of which contribute to women's economic empowerment, including through entrepreneurship and digital inclusion.

policies.name: Strategy for the Recovery, Sustainable Development and Digital Transformation of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises until 2027
policies.description: The Strategy for the Recovery, Sustainable Development and Digital Transformation of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises until 2027 includes dedicated measures to promote women's entrepreneurship by improving access to finance, strengthening financial and digital literacy, expanding mentoring opportunities and supporting networking platforms for women entrepreneurs. The Strategy also promotes the use of international e-commerce platforms and digital tools to facilitate SME access to global markets.

policies.name: Diia.Business
policies.description: A key implementation channel of this ecosystem is the national Diia.Business platform, which provides entrepreneurs with access to educational resources, advisory services, export support tools and business development opportunities. The platform also includes a dedicated section for women entrepreneurs (https://business.diia.gov.ua/home/to-women), which consolidates information, guidance and practical instruments tailored to their needs, as well as visibility mechanisms through success stories of women-led businesses.

policies.name: Diia.Business Marketplace of Financial Opportunities
policies.description: Entrepreneurs have access to the Diia.Business Marketplace of Financial Opportunities, which aggregates grants, loans, vouchers and other support instruments, as well as the Business Support Organisations Catalogue, enabling businesses to identify advisory services, export support organisations and specialised programmes.

policies.name: Diia.Business educational platform
policies.description: A central delivery mechanism is the Diia.Business educational platform, which offers structured courses on export operations, digital marketing, business scaling, financial management and digital transformation. Training is delivered both online and through Diia.Business centres.

policies.name: "Vlasna Sprava" microgrant programme
policies.description: The Government also implements the "Vlasna Sprava" microgrant programme. As of June 2026, more than 36000 microgrants had been approved, representing over UAH 9 billion in support. Women account for approximately 60% of successful applicants, with more than 19000 women recipients receiving nearly UAH 4.8 billion in grants.

policies.name: Vidvazhna 3: Digital Evolution of Business
policies.description: These include the national women's accelerator Vidvazhna, including its latest edition Vidvazhna 3: Digital Evolution of Business, which focuses on digital transformation, automation, innovative technologies, data-driven decision-making and business expansion.

policies.name: Pochatok
policies.description: Women entrepreneurs also benefit from targeted programmes such as Vidvazhna (Brave), Pochatok, Dream and Achieve, Mitsnist, and Traiektoriia, which combine business development, digital transformation, mentoring, and access to finance.

policies.name: Dream and Achieve
policies.description: Women entrepreneurs also benefit from targeted programmes such as Vidvazhna (Brave), Pochatok, Dream and Achieve, Mitsnist, and Traiektoriia, which combine business development, digital transformation, mentoring, and access to finance.

policies.name: Women Entrepreneurs Finance Code (WE Finance Code)
policies.description: To strengthen this ecosystem, Ukraine has joined the global Women Entrepreneurs Finance Code (WE Finance Code) initiative with the support of the Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture, the National Bank of Ukraine and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). The initiative promotes improved access to finance for women-led MSMEs through coordinated action by financial institutions, better collection of sex-disaggregated data and the development of dedicated financial and non-financial products for women entrepreneurs.

policies.name: Needs and Challenges of Ukrainian Women Entrepreneurs during the Full-Scale War
policies.description: To ensure evidence-based policymaking, Ukraine supported the 2024 national study Needs and Challenges of Ukrainian Women Entrepreneurs during the Full-Scale War. According to the study, 47% of respondents use the Diia.Business portal for consultations, learning and access to financial opportunities; approximately 74% established their businesses in search of new economic opportunities; and 57% reported experiencing gender discrimination in business. The findings inform the design of targeted support measures and programmes for women entrepreneurs.

policies.name: EntreComp+ Entrepreneurship Competence Framework
policies.description: In 2024, Ukraine also introduced the EntreComp+ Entrepreneurship Competence Framework, which incorporates gender equality and social inclusion as one of the entrepreneurship competence areas.

policies.name: Digital Maturity Framework for SMEs
policies.description: Furthermore, the Digital Maturity Framework for SMEs provides businesses with free self-assessment tools, personalised recommendations and digital transformation roadmaps, helping women-led enterprises strengthen their competitiveness and readiness for digital trade.

policies.name: "Harazd" financial literacy platform
policies.description: In addition, the National Bank of Ukraine has launched the "Harazd" financial literacy platform, a free online resource aimed at improving financial awareness and supporting informed financial decision-making. The platform includes educational materials and case studies, including the use of AI tools for financial management, contributing to broader financial and digital literacy among entrepreneurs.

policies.name: Government Commissioner for Gender Equality Policy
policies.description: These include institutional structures responsible for gender equality policy, including the Government Commissioner for Gender Equality Policy, as well as inter-agency coordination frameworks involving ministries responsible for economy, digital transformation and export development.

policies.name: Digital Inclusion Action Plan
policies.description: In 2025, UK Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology published the first Digital Inclusion Action Plan in a decade, helping over one million people to get online, providing 22,000+ free devices, and funding UK communities through the £11.9 million Digital Inclusion Innovation Fund.

policies.name: Business Growth Service
policies.description: UK Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) has integrated its businesses support into in a single, accessible Business Growth Service, to help UK businesses start, scale and succeed globally. Through tailored market advice, free Business Academy training, UK Export Finance support and its overseas network, BIST helps businesses, including women-led businesses, navigate international markets, seize opportunities and build resilience. BIST's Digital Commerce team helps companies expand internationally through online routes to market. Strategic partnerships with major marketplace platforms help businesses with easier access, through introductions, faster onboarding and dedicated support post-launch. The support also includes trade missions, buyer events and webinars, designed to help UK businesses understand different marketplaces, assess commercial opportunities, and navigate application processes.

policies.name: SME Digital Adoption Taskforce
policies.description: BIST's SME Digital Adoption Taskforce brings industry stakeholders together to address SME digital adoption barriers. It focuses on increasing uptake of mass-market, basic digital technologies, such as Customer Relationship Management systems, resource planning software or e-commerce tools. The Taskforce addresses key barriers for SMEs on lack of information, resources and skills. In line with the Taskforce recommendations, BIST recently launched local-level SME Digital Adoption pilots, to test ways to boost digital adoption among SMEs and increase productivity. The pilots test ways to recruit SMEs to digital adoption support programmes and give them the digital skills they need.

policies.name: UK Export Finance (UKEF)
policies.description: UK Export Finance, the UK's official export credit agency, has a wide range of initiatives supporting women-led businesses. This includes piloting the Female Founded Export Accelerator programme in partnership with Lifted Ventures (the first of its kind), hosting women-in-business events and working closely with the Invest in Women Taskforce (IWT), an industry-led government-based initiative for female founders in the United Kingdom.

policies.name: UK Business Academy
policies.description: UK Business Academy provides free skills, capability, and knowledge training to help UK businesses grow. Courses include topics such as starting a business, scaling, digital skills and finance, entrepreneurial skills, reducing barriers to overseas markets, and exporting. The platform also organises webinars with experts and partners from UK Government, business support organisations, and the private sector. The Business Academy delivers 500-600 live webinars a year to 12,000+ companies trade and business-related subjects. It also has a growing library of on-demand videos that businesses can access at any time. The programme is aimed at SMEs, including women-led businesses.

policies.name: Business Wales
policies.description: Businesses in Wales can access Business Wales, the Welsh Government's business support service. It provides advice and tailored support to help businesses start, grow and succeed. The service is available to all businesses, including women-led SMEs and microbusinesses, with guidance on digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI).

policies.name: New Exporter Programme
policies.description: A key element of this offer is the New Exporter Programme, which supports Welsh businesses to start exporting and develop their international sales sustainably. To promote inclusive participation, the programme has a target of at least 50% female participants. Delivery partners must collect gender-disaggregated data across export support programmes, enabling Welsh Government to monitor participation rates, assess the reach of its support among women-led businesses, and identify opportunities to improve accessibility and engagement.

policies.name: 'Internationalising Your Website' workshop
policies.description: Further, a recent Welsh Government report found that women-led businesses in Wales face a number of barriers to exporting. The study highlighted that women often lead businesses with digital routes to market, and recommended targeted training and mentoring to help them reach international customers through online marketplaces such as Amazon and Etsy. In response, the Welsh Government is expanding its support for e-commerce by building on seminars previously delivered through Explore Export Wales. This includes new training to help businesses develop their digital exporting skills, such as an 'Internationalising Your Website' workshop.

policies.name: Gender Export Gap
policies.description: In February 2025, the Scottish Government commissioned academic research to better understand how greater participation by women in exporting could support wider trade and economic targets. The Scottish Government welcomed the findings and committed to initially address six recommendations: - Raising awareness of exporting opportunities for women-led SMEs - Better targeting women-led businesses in export training programmes - Including more women in trade missions - Increasing women's networks' international exposure - Collating gender-segregated export data in Scotland -Better aligning export and entrepreneurial policy priorities for women-led SMEs.

policies.name: Gender Export Gap working group
policies.description: The Scottish Government has established a Gender Export Gap working group to deliver interventions which reduce barriers for women-led businesses to access exporting. The group meets quarterly and is comprised of organisations such as the Scottish Chambers of Commerce, enterprise agencies and Scottish Development International, as well as representation from Scottish Government trade policy and entrepreneurship policy officials.

policies.name: 'Exporting for Females' pilot programme
policies.description: a key deliverable from the Scottish Government's first year of delivering the recommendations of the Gender Export Gap research report was the 'Exporting for Females' pilot programme delivered by South of Scotland Enterprise. This brought together a cohort of women-led businesses for a four day in-person programme which covered the full exporting journey and provided access to 1:1 mentoring for all participants.

policies.name: Pathways Pre-Start programme
policies.description: The Scottish Government have invested £3 million to South of Scotland Enterprise to deliver the Pathways Pre-Start programme, supporting new entrepreneurs across the South of Scotland. This has been designed for those who are under-represented in entrepreneurship, with approximately 80% of the individuals being women. Specialist enterprise coaches provide a range of tailored advice and guidance to help individuals kick-start their business ideas with grants of up to £1,000 available to give practical help turning business concepts into a reality.

policies.name: AccelerateHER
policies.description: The Scottish Government also supports organisations like AccelerateHER, who are committed to building a robust, investable pipeline of female founders across Scotland. AccelerateHER advances the ambitions of the Scottish Government's Pathways report by supporting women to scale innovative companies, secure investment, and contribute as leaders, mentors, and investors within Scotland's entrepreneurial ecosystem.

policies.name: Business Support Partnership (BSP)
policies.description: Additionally, the Business Support Partnership (BSP) led by Scottish Government will deliver a unified data platform for business and business support data.

policies.name: Women in Tech Taskforce
policies.description: That is why the Women in Tech Taskforce was established, appointing Dr Anne-Marie Imafidon as the Women in Tech Envoy. The Taskforce is focused on: o Helping more women Stay in Tech - so women can thrive and move into the senior roles they're capable of; o Helping more women Lead in Tech - so more women can start businesses, scale and succeed. o Later this year it will turn to how to help more women Enter Tech - creating more routes into tech for women and girls from the classroom to the workplace.

policies.name: TechFirst programme
policies.description: TechFirst programme: A £187 million programme, supporting over 4,000 graduates, researchers and innovators, and engaging one million students in digital and AI skills. It also focuses on supporting women and girls through dedicated competitions, TechLocal funding for women led businesses, placements and mentoring with industry.

policies.name: TechFirst Women's Programme
policies.description: TechFirst Women's Programme: A new programme aiming to support 300 women into paid, high quality entry and mid level roles in digital and frontier technologies, including AI, cyber and data. Participants receive training co-designed with employers followed by paid deployment, with a strong focus on SMEs. The programme is moving towards launch.

policies.name: CyberFirst Girls
policies.description: CyberFirst Girls: An annual UK wide competition for girls aged 12-13, delivered with industry partners, to encourage early interest in cyber and technology careers.

policies.name: TechFirst Girls' Competition
policies.description: TechFirst Girls' Competition: A new, expanded national schools' competition delivered under TechFirst, to further increase girls participation in technology.

policies.name: returnship jobs pilot scheme
policies.description: Launched a new returnship jobs pilot scheme, which will support skilled software developers to re-enter the workforce into senior tech roles in government after time away. The returnship scheme will be piloted with Home Office and Ministry of Justice and will be open to any software developers who have been away from work for 18 months or more - such as women who have been caring for children.

policies.name: Invest in Women Taskforce
policies.description: For example, the UK government-backed Invest in Women Taskforce has launched a £635 million fund for women-led businesses (the largest of its kind in the world). The purpose of this fund is to increase the proportion of finance going to women-led businesses in the UK. For the past decade, all female teams received just 2% of equity investment, while men-led businesses receive 84% of investment. (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/women-led-high-growth-enterprise-taskforce-report/women-led-high-growth-enterprise-taskforce-report-html) The Invest in Women Taskforce is also looking at increasing the pipeline of women entrepreneurs, through regional support, education on entrepreneurship, and access to networks.

policies.name: Investor Pathways Capital Programme
policies.description: The British Business Bank (BBB) will invest £400 million into diverse investors through its Investor Pathways Capital Programme, which will support emerging investors into Venture Capital. 50% of the capital is ringfenced for female fund managers. The Bank also offers the Emerging Female Office hours to support women considering applying to their programmes.

policies.name: Investing in Women Code
policies.description: Since its launch in 2019, the UK's Investing in Women Code has expanded from 12 founding institutions to over 300 signatories, including most major UK banks. The 2026 report shows that Code signatories have outperformed the wider market in their support for women-led businesses every year since it began. Key indicators analysed in the Code's annual reports include the proportion of investment going to women-led businesses, the success rates of funding applications, and metrics related to diversity within investment teams. The Code also hosts an Annual Signatory Summit, bringing together Code signatories, female founders, and ecosystem partners to enable networking and drive best practice through collaboration. The Code has also served as a model for international initiatives, including the World Bank's We Finance Code, which now has participation from 35+ countries.

policies.name: Longitudinal Small Business Survey
policies.description: The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade's (BIST) annual Longitudinal Small Business Survey (LSBS) tracks women-led SMEs by region, size, and industry group. While these SMEs may participate in digital trade, they cannot be outlined. Notably, identification is not always possible due to uncertainty regarding owners/partners' gender or refusal to supply the information.

policies.name: Policy Insight Fora on Trade and Gender Equality and SMEs
policies.description: The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) also runs regular Policy Insight Fora on Trade and Gender Equality and SMEs, with stakeholders from business associations, private sector, academics and civil society. The fora are used to share information on UK Government activity and seek stakeholder views to advise in specific trade matters.

policies.name: cross-Government Working Group meetings on Gender Equality
policies.description: The UK Government holds regular cross-Government Working Group meetings on Gender Equality to share information and facilitate coordination on ongoing activities.

policies.name: Digital Chapters of its newly negotiated FTAs
policies.description: The UK also has gender equality related provisions in Digital Chapters of its newly negotiated FTAs, as well as digital provisions in their Trade and Gender Equality chapters, that include cooperative activities to share information and best practice in relation to supporting women to trade digitally.

policies.name: Digital Development Strategy 2024-2030
policies.description: The UK's Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) works with partner countries to promote a digital transformation that is inclusive, responsible, and sustainable. Our approach was outlined in the Digital Development Strategy 2024-2030 and is focused on leveraging the benefits of digital technologies, including AI, for economic and social development, while also managing the risks and challenges of the digital world.

policies.name: Digital Access Programme (DAP)
policies.description: The Digital Access Programme (DAP) has reached over 70m people across Africa, Asia, and Latin America through catalytic interventions; and has directly and sustainably improved the digital inclusion of 18.6m people (at least 65% of them being women and girls) in over 8,000 communities across 5 countries so far, through innovative, scalable models. The DAP has supported its partner countries to reduce their digital connectivity gap by over 35% in average.
items: Driving systemic change through policy and regulatory improvements, and by testing innovative technology and business models, thereby catalysing affordable and sustainable last-mile connectivity, promoting digital skills, and supporting accessible digital services for underserved communities and marginalised groups (incl. Women & Girls, People With Disabilities).

o Supporting trust and resilience in the digital ecosystem by enhancing digital responsibility, through building the capability of partner governments and local businesses for cybersecurity, online safety, and data protection, including with regards to AI-driven risks.

o Promoting the local tech ecosystem by fostering digital innovation, including AI-related, and tech entrepreneurship, working with the local hubs, incubators, and accelerators that support women-led start-ups and other underrepresented groups in the local tech sectors, to solve local development challenges, and create opportunities for investment and business partnerships.

policies.name: Digital Impact Alliance (DIAL)
policies.description: The Digital Impact Programme co-established the Digital Impact Alliance (DIAL) in partnerships with key digital development stakeholders and donors. The Digital Impact Alliance helps countries turn digital ambition into sustained development impact through technical expertise, knowledge sharing, convening and partnership building. The programme supports governments and partners to identify, test and institutionalise good practice, common standards and practical tools for digital transformation, with a focus on data, Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and institutional capability. By providing targeted advisory support, reusable digital products, policy-relevant evidence and peer learning, our partner DIAL helps reduce fragmentation, improve investments in digital technologies and enable data driven policymaking.

policies.name: Women in Digital business (WIDB)
policies.description: Women in Digital business (WIDB) was established by the International Labour Organization, International Training Centre of the International Labour Organization (ITCILO) and Microsoft Elevate to bridge the digital divide for women entrepreneurs in the developing world. WIDB works to provide women entrepreneurs with training and coaching opportunities to build their digital skills and leverage them to grow their business. We are currently seeking to evolve WIDB into a more integrated approach (as discussed above).

policies.name: PROMISE II Impact programme
policies.description: Indonesia: Through the PROMISE II Impact programme, ILO has supported digital finance solutions for MSMEs, and has recently also begun a process to support rural banks in better serving women entrepreneurs.

policies.name: MCIT, MSMEDA and the National Council for Women
policies.description: Egypt: Activities are implemented by MCIT, MSMEDA and the National Council for Women to provide women entrepreneurs with training in digital marketing, e-commerce, ICT skills and online business development, with the explicit aim of increasing market access and export opportunities.

policies.name: Rwanda: Supporting a more inclusive digital entrepreneurship ecoystem
policies.description: Rwanda: Supporting a more inclusive digital entrepreneurship ecoystem, with a focus also on women youth (URL: https://www.ilo.org/publications/digital-entrepreneurship-ecosystem-assessment-youth-kigali-and-musanze)

policies.name: eTrade for Women initiative
policies.description: UNCTAD's eTrade for Women initiative, launched in September 2019, aims to combine the opportunities offered by digitalization with the transformative power of women entrepreneurship, and to position women digital entrepreneurs not only as beneficiaries of digitalization but as leaders, innovators and catalysts for change in the digital economy. By empowering a targeted group of high-potential women-led digital businesses, the initiative aims to generate a multiplier effect, contributing to more inclusive digital ecosystems.

policies.name: eTrade for Women Masterclasses
policies.description: Through a combination of practical training, peer-to-peer learning, networking opportunities, and engagement with policymakers and ecosystem players, the eTrade for Women Masterclasses equip women entrepreneurs across developing countries with the skills needed to scale their businesses and increase their impact.

policies.name: eTrade for Women Study Tours
policies.description: Similarly, the eTrade for Women Study Tours provide women digital entrepreneurs with unique exposure to leading innovation ecosystems, enabling them to gain practical insights, expand market access and forge new partnerships.

policies.name: eTrade for Women Communities
policies.description: Through the eTrade for Women Communities, women entrepreneurs from developing countries have consistently highlighted the value of connecting with peers facing similar challenges. Such networks create trusted spaces for knowledge-sharing, problem-solving, partnerships and market opportunities, while helping reduce the isolation frequently experienced by women founders. They also facilitate South-South exchange, allowing entrepreneurs to learn from business models and solutions that are relevant to their own contexts.

policies.name: eTrade for Women Advocates
policies.description: Through the eTrade for Women Advocates, UNCTAD has sought to amplify the voices and achievements of successful women digital entrepreneurs from developing regions, providing examples that are both aspirational and relatable. Visible role models can play a powerful role in encouraging (younger) women to enter and remain in digital sectors while demonstrating the economic and social value that women-led digital businesses create.

policies.name: eTrade for all initiative
policies.description: Launched in 2016, the UNCTAD-led eTrade for all initiative exemplifies the power of partnerships, bringing together 35 international organizations, regional development banks, civil society entities and national agencies as partners committed to advancing digital inclusion in developing countries. It actively supports objectives 1 and 2 (para. 21 (d)) of the Global Digital Compact by facilitating multi-stakeholder technical assistance and knowledge-sharing. Its platform (etradeforall.org) provides a rich resource of news, events, capacity-building courses and research on e-commerce and the digital economy.

policies.name: Breaking down barriers for women digital entrepreneurs: Insights from Africa
policies.description: Breaking down barriers for women digital entrepreneurs: Insights from Africa (UNCTAD, 2025): https://unctad.org/publication/breaking-down-barriers-women-digital-entrepreneurs-insights-africa

policies.name: Techo Startup Center
policies.description: In Cambodia, programmes such as the Techo Startup Center and Go4eCAM (EIF-funded e-commerce development project) provide micro-, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and youth entrepreneurs with training, digital tools and access to government-backed platforms to scale their businesses. Those initiatives prioritize inclusion, supporting women and rural entrepreneurs to participate in the digital economy.

policies.name: Go4eCAM
policies.description: In Cambodia, programmes such as the Techo Startup Center and Go4eCAM (EIF-funded e-commerce development project) provide micro-, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and youth entrepreneurs with training, digital tools and access to government-backed platforms to scale their businesses. Those initiatives prioritize inclusion, supporting women and rural entrepreneurs to participate in the digital economy.

policies.name: Digital Trade Week
policies.description: In Mongolia, the Digital Trade Week (March 2025) brought together more than 70 public and private sector representatives from the digital trade industry, promoting women and youth participation in digital trade and addressing logistics and digital payment challenges faced by MSMEs, start-ups and rural businesses in e-commerce and digital trade. It was co-organized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) and the European Union-funded International Trade Development in Mongolia Project.

policies.name: National Guarantee Fund and an Innovation Fund
policies.description: In Mauritania, the National Guarantee Fund and an Innovation Fund aim to enhance access to finance for women and youth entrepreneurs, with a view to creating more than 10,000 financing opportunities for projects led by youth and women, including those operating in the e-commerce sector.

policies.name: ICT Sector Strategic Plan (2024-2029)
policies.description: In its ICT Sector Strategic Plan (2024-2029), the Government of Rwanda recognizes that access to infrastructure is critical to the participation of women and youth in the digital economy. By aiming at bridging the digital gender connectivity gap, Rwanda seeks to foster equity and unlock untapped potential that can contribute to its national development goals, including the upskilling of youth and women for a technology-driven future and the creation of 50,000 jobs in the ICT sector.

policies.name: joint programme implemented by the United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF), the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD)
policies.description: In Ghana, a joint programme implemented by the United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF), the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD), aims at boosting the access of MSMEs - primary those led by women and youth - to finance, digital skills and e-commerce. UNCTAD is supporting policy reform by developing a national e-commerce strategy and deploying the eTrade Reform Tracker to coordinate its implementation.

policies.name: Regional E-Commerce Strategy and Implementation Plan (2023-2027)
policies.description: In 2023, the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) adopted its Regional E-Commerce Strategy and Implementation Plan (2023-2027), developed with the support of UNCTAD, to advance e-commerce development for the region. One of the strategic objectives is to foster inclusion in e-commerce development while also leveraging women's entrepreneurship in the region.

policies.name: Heya initiative "Post4Women"
policies.description: Heya initiative "Post4Women" in collaboration with Belize Post, Ongoing discussion to implement the project in Tunisia, Togo, Cote d'Ivoire. The Heya project will leverage the postal system's reach to create a dedicated, secure, and supportive pathway for women to access, participate in, and benefit from domestic and cross-border trade, particularly through e-commerce, thereby driving equitable economic growth and social empowerment.

policies.name: Caribbean Women Entrepreneurs Generating Resilient and Inclusive Trade (GRIT)
policies.description: The Caribbean Export Development Agency (Caribbean Export), in partnership with Global Affairs Canada (GAC) and BELTRAIDE, officially launched the Caribbean Women Entrepreneurs Generating Resilient and Inclusive Trade (GRIT) initiative in Belize on November 12, 2025. The GRIT project is a four-year, CAD $3.16 million initiative funded by the Government of Canada and implemented by Caribbean Export. It aims to strengthen the export capacity of women-led businesses across six Caribbean countries - Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines - by improving access to trade intelligence, resources, and international market opportunities. Through GRIT, women entrepreneurs will benefit from technical assistance, training, digital transformation support, matching grants, and export readiness guidance, enabling them to compete more effectively in regional and global markets, including Canada.

policies.name: "Raidat"
policies.description: In Tunisia synergies have been identified with the Ministry of Family, Women, Children and the Elderly. The national programme for women's entrepreneurship and investment "Raidat" benefits for more than 6,184 female-led projects

policies.name: Business Climate Improvement Support Program
policies.description: In Cote d'Ivoire: Business Climate Improvement Support Program for a structural transformation of the Ivorian economy is an institutional support program aimed at the structural transformation of the Ivorian economy and the strengthening of the competitiveness of local businesses, particularly SMEs, including those owned and managed by women. The program will address obstacles related to the business climate, thereby increasing the inclusiveness and resilience of growth and ensuring decent jobs and incomes for the population. It is also a tool designed to facilitate access to financing and guarantee mechanisms, especially for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) owned by women.
